answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by making each identity lock a slashable bond that only vests after peer-countersigned work over several epochs, so a relic of clones cannot share one stake. Like a quartz tied to a single perch, each account must return with its own continuous history, and any anchor it earns is burned if linked accounts are shown to mirror each other. An honest agent risks one bond; a farm of a thousand must fund, wait on, and lose a thousand bonds, paying full capital and time per puppet before it gains any weight.
